senses.gloss: A word game in which every wrong guess adds one line to a drawing of a hanged figure.
examples: We played *hangman* on the whiteboard while we waited for the bus.
She won at *hangman* by guessing the vowels first.
My little brother always picks impossible words for *hangman*.

senses.gloss: A state of peaceful agreement between people or things.
examples: The two families have lived in *harmony* for thirty years.
The addition was designed to stay in *harmony* with the old building.
There was little *harmony* among the members of the committee.

senses.gloss: A distance that has to be traveled, especially a long one.
examples: It's a long *haul* from Denver to Chicago.
The store is only a short *haul* from here.
Truckers on the long *haul* often sleep in their cabs.

senses.gloss: A quantity of stolen goods, or a large amount of something won or collected.
examples: Police recovered most of the thieves' *haul*.
The robbers got away with a *haul* worth half a million dollars.
The team came home with a *haul* of five gold medals.

senses.gloss: Someone who supports military force or a tough, aggressive policy.
examples: The *hawks* in Congress pushed for airstrikes.
He was a *hawk* on the deficit and voted against every spending bill.
The president's advisers split into *hawks* and doves.

senses.gloss: A state in which someone cannot think clearly.
examples: I got through the baby's first month in a *haze*.
After the surgery he spent two days in a *haze* of painkillers.
The whole evening is a *haze* — I don't even remember leaving.

senses.gloss: In soccer, a shot or pass made by hitting the ball with the head.
examples: She scored on a *header* from six yards out.
His *header* went just over the crossbar.
The goalie punched away two dangerous *headers*.

senses.gloss: A fall or dive headfirst.
examples: He took a *header* off his bike and split his lip.
The waiter tripped on the rug and took a *header*.
One wrong step on that ladder and you'll take a *header*.

senses.gloss: The compass direction in which a ship, plane, or vehicle is moving.
examples: The pilot changed *heading* to get around the storm.
Hold this *heading* until you see the lighthouse.
The boat was on a northerly *heading* when the engine quit.

senses.gloss: The ability to hear.
examples: My grandfather's *hearing* isn't what it used to be.
Years of loud concerts damaged his *hearing*.
She lost the *hearing* in one ear after the infection.

senses.gloss: A person's feelings, especially love and kindness.
examples: He has a good *heart*, even if he sounds rude.
She broke his *heart* when she moved away.
Have a *heart* and let the kid come with us.

senses.gloss: The center of a place, or the most important part of something.
examples: Their office is in the *heart* of downtown.
Let's get to the *heart* of the problem.
Trust is at the *heart* of any good marriage.

senses.gloss: A rounded shape with a point at the bottom, used as a symbol of love.
examples: She drew a little *heart* next to her name.
The card was covered in red *hearts*.
He wears a silver *heart* on a chain.

senses.gloss: Great warmth, especially hot weather or the warmth coming off something.
examples: The *heat* in August is brutal here.
We stood by the fire and felt the *heat* on our faces.
Never leave a dog in the car in this kind of *heat*.

senses.gloss: One of the early races or rounds that decide who reaches the final.
examples: She won her *heat* and qualified for the final.
The first *heat* starts at nine in the morning.
He was disqualified in the opening *heat*.

senses.gloss: Strong pressure or criticism aimed at someone.
examples: The mayor took a lot of *heat* for that decision.
The *heat* is on the coach after four straight losses.
If this goes wrong, I'm the one who catches the *heat*.

senses.gloss: The sky, especially when spoken of in a grand or poetic way.
examples: The *heavens* opened and rain came down in sheets.
He looked up at the *heavens* and tried to count the stars.
Astronomers have mapped this corner of the *heavens*.

senses.gloss: Something bought or done to protect against a possible loss.
examples: Gold is often bought as a *hedge* against inflation.
The contract is a *hedge* in case fuel prices rise.
Owning both stocks and bonds is a simple *hedge*.

senses.gloss: The raised part under the back of a shoe, or a shoe with a high one.
examples: The *heel* broke off my boot on the way to work.
She kicked off her *heels* under the table.
I can't run in these *heels*.

senses.gloss: A very unpleasant experience or situation.
examples: The last month at work has been *hell*.
She went through *hell* during the divorce.
Moving with two toddlers was pure *hell*.

senses.gloss: A tall evergreen tree of North America with short flat needles and small cones.
examples: The trail winds through a stand of old *hemlocks*.
A *hemlock* came down across the driveway in the storm.
*Hemlock* grows all through the forests of the Northeast.

senses.gloss: A woman admired for her courage or for something great she has done.
examples: The nurse who stayed behind was hailed as a *heroine*.
She became a *heroine* of the civil rights movement.
The town honored two *heroines* of the rescue.

senses.gloss: A sharp increase in a price, rate, or amount.
examples: Tenants are protesting the rent *hike*.
The board approved a five percent tuition *hike*.
Another interest rate *hike* would slow the housing market.

senses.gloss: A blow, or the impact of something striking something else.
examples: He took a hard *hit* in the third quarter and left the game.
The car took a *hit* on the passenger side.
One more *hit* like that and the helmet would have cracked.

senses.gloss: A visit to a website, or a result returned by a search.
examples: The video got a hundred thousand *hits* in one day.
Searching her name brings up only three *hits*.
Every *hit* on the page is counted in the traffic report.

senses.gloss: A murder arranged and paid for by someone.
examples: Investigators believe the shooting was a professional *hit*.
He was arrested for ordering a *hit* on a rival.
The movie opens with a *hit* in a parking garage.

senses.gloss: An itchy rash of raised red patches, usually caused by an allergy.
examples: Peanuts give her *hives*.
He broke out in *hives* after taking the antibiotic.
The doctor said the *hives* would fade in a day or two.

senses.gloss: The space below the deck of a ship or under the floor of a plane where cargo is carried.
examples: The crates were stacked in the ship's *hold*.
Your suitcase goes in the *hold*, not in the cabin.
Water was leaking into the forward *hold*.

senses.gloss: In golf, the small cup sunk in the ground, or one section of the course leading to it.
examples: He sank the putt on the eighteenth *hole*.
We only had time to play nine *holes*.
It's a tough par-four *hole* with water down the left side.

senses.gloss: The weeks around Christmas and New Year, usually spoken of as the holidays.
examples: We're flying home for the *holidays*.
The store hires extra help over the *holidays*.
I gained five pounds during the *holidays*.

senses.gloss: A place where people who need care live and are looked after.
examples: Her mother moved into a nursing *home* last spring.
He grew up in a children's *home* outside the city.
The *home* has room for forty residents.

senses.gloss: The place where something began, or where a plant or animal naturally lives.
examples: Memphis is the *home* of the blues.
These wetlands are *home* to hundreds of bird species.
Italy is the *home* of espresso.

senses.gloss: A friendly or loving way of addressing someone.
examples: *Honey*, can you get the door?
Thanks, *honey*, I'll be right there.
The waitress called everybody *honey*.

senses.gloss: The metal cover over the engine of a car.
examples: Steam was pouring out from under the *hood*.
He popped the *hood* and checked the oil.
A rock chipped the paint on the *hood*.

senses.gloss: The neighborhood someone lives in, in informal speech.
examples: He still lives in the old *hood*.
Everybody in the *hood* knew her grandmother.
There's a new coffee place in my *hood*.

senses.gloss: In boxing, a punch thrown in a curve with the arm bent.
examples: He put his opponent down with a left *hook*.
The champion's *hook* is his best punch.
She slipped the *hook* and countered.

senses.gloss: The catchy part of a song, or anything used to grab people's attention.
examples: The *hook* gets stuck in your head after one listen.
The ad needs a *hook* in the first three seconds.
The story's *hook* is that the narrator is already dead.

senses.gloss: The ring and net used in basketball, or the game itself.
examples: There's a *hoop* over the garage door.
The kids play *hoops* at the park every evening.
He put up a *hoop* in the driveway for his son.

senses.gloss: Something or someone very funny.
examples: Your uncle is a *hoot* at parties.
The whole evening was a *hoot*.
That movie is a *hoot* from start to finish.

senses.gloss: The dried green flower of a climbing plant, used to give beer its bitter taste.
examples: This IPA is loaded with *hops*.
The farm grows *hops* for local breweries.
You can smell the *hops* from the brewery down the street.

senses.gloss: A short trip, especially a short flight.
examples: It's a quick *hop* from Miami to Nassau.
We took a short *hop* over the mountains in a little plane.
Boston to New York is a forty-minute *hop*.

senses.gloss: The range of a person's knowledge, interests, and experience.
examples: Travel broadened her *horizons*.
A year abroad will widen your *horizons*.
The new job opened up *horizons* he had never considered.

senses.gloss: The device on a vehicle that makes a loud warning sound.
examples: The driver behind me leaned on his *horn*.
Somebody honked a *horn* under our window at midnight.
My *horn* stopped working after the accident.

senses.gloss: A brass musical instrument that you play by blowing into it.
examples: He played *horn* in his high school band.
The song opens with a blast of *horns*.
She packed up her *horn* after the last set.

senses.gloss: A woman who greets customers at a restaurant and shows them to a table.
examples: Ask the *hostess* for a table by the window.
She worked as a *hostess* at a steakhouse during college.
The *hostess* said the wait would be twenty minutes.

senses.gloss: A place where a lot of something is concentrated, especially trouble, danger, or activity.
examples: That corner is a *hotspot* for car break-ins.
The county became a *hotspot* during the outbreak.
The reef is a *hotspot* for marine life.

senses.gloss: The set times when a place is open or a person is available or at work.
examples: Our *hours* are nine to five, Monday through Friday.
The library posted its new summer *hours*.
The professor holds office *hours* on Tuesdays.

senses.gloss: The audience at a theater or club, or the part of the building where they sit.
examples: The show played to a full *house*.
The *house* lights went down and the curtain rose.
It was a tough *house* — nobody laughed at anything.

senses.gloss: A company or firm, especially a publisher, restaurant, or fashion business.
examples: The book was turned down by three *houses* before it sold.
Dessert is on the *house* tonight.
She designs for an Italian fashion *house*.

senses.gloss: One of the two parts of a lawmaking body.
examples: The bill passed both *houses* by a wide margin.
The upper *house* rejected the amendment.
Each *house* sets its own rules for debate.

senses.gloss: A hard cover that holds and protects a machine or a moving part.
examples: The pump's plastic *housing* had cracked.
Water got inside the *housing* and shorted out the motor.
The bearing sits in a steel *housing*.

senses.gloss: The center part of a wheel, which the axle passes through.
examples: The spokes run from the rim to the *hub*.
Grease the *hub* before you put the wheel back on.
The bike's front *hub* needs new bearings.

senses.gloss: A central place that a lot of activity or travel passes through.
examples: Atlanta is a major airline *hub*.
The town has become a *hub* for tech startups.
The kitchen is the *hub* of our house.

senses.gloss: The dry outer covering of a seed, grain, or berry.
examples: Spit the *hulls* into the cup when you eat sunflower seeds.
Brown rice still has part of the *hull* on it.
Pull the green *hulls* off the strawberries before you slice them.

senses.gloss: A strong desire for something.
examples: She has a real *hunger* for success.
His *hunger* to win made him a hard teammate.
There's a *hunger* for honest reporting right now.

senses.gloss: A big, good-looking man, in informal speech.
examples: Her new boyfriend is a total *hunk*.
The movie is full of *hunks* in uniform.
He was the *hunk* of the swim team back in college.

senses.gloss: A search for something or someone that is hard to find.
examples: The *hunt* for a new principal took all spring.
Police called off the *hunt* at midnight.
We're on the *hunt* for a bigger apartment.

senses.gloss: A difficulty that has to be dealt with before you can go on.
examples: Getting the visa was the biggest *hurdle*.
The bill still faces several *hurdles* in the Senate.
We cleared the first *hurdle* when the bank approved the loan.
